value.headline: What A Blue Wave Looks Like In Texas, Day By Day
value.claim: Pre-registered tests: top-30 daily EV >=25% above 2022; blue share (12 Biden-2020 counties / top 30) >=69% AND climbing = wave; 67-68 ordinary; <67 Rs not depressed
value.evidence: Computed on SOS: top-30 daily in-person 1.70x, 1.58x, 1.56x, 1.50x, 1.48x of 2022 (passes). Blue share Days 1-5: 69.9, 69.7, 69.6, 69.5, 68.6 raw (~69.3 lag-adjusted): LEVEL passes; flat to slightly down rather than climbing (the drop sits inside the Harris reporting lag), while it ROSE through EV in 2018 (67.9 -> 69.6), 2022 (67.6 -> 68.2) and 2024 (65.8 -> 66.9). The author's 'and climbing' condition is not met so far. A county share measures turnout, not vote choice.

value.headline: 'So far there is zero blue wave'
value.claim: 18M early votes; D-R 47-30 vs 48-32 at the same date of 2022, 'virtually identical'; 'Dems flood polls on first day, Reps usually catch up'
value.evidence: Pooled numbers hold: the 22-state party set is D+14.7 vs D+12.2 (2022) on the same day, ten days out. State by state NC is far more D (D+17.5 vs D+7.8); IA, AZ, PA, NV and ME are at or below 2022. value: No single post from Baris makes the whole claim as the theory states it [V, all 773 in-window posts read]. Nothing he posted says "Democrats flood the first week, riding positive coverage, to depress Republicans." He never wrote "Beto" in a post in the window.

The core D-early / R-late contrast is his, in his own posts [V]: Democrats are banking low-propensity and new voters (people who did not vote in 2024) early. Republicans vote later, or rely on reliable voters on Election Day. He says outright that parties turn out their low-propensity voters early so they can spend Election Day resources on reliable voters.

The Beto/Cruz comparison is something he said on his own X broadcast, not in a text post [V video page; R machine captions; I speaker]. The broadcast is "Barnes and Baris Episode 120: What Are the Odds?", posted on X Oct 12, 2026 (status 2109750958813237702). It is at 2:03:41 in the YouTube copy of the same stream. He is relaying what a Democratic pollster told him about Texas. The comparison: like Cruz vs Beto, Talarico will win the early vote big, and everyone will then wait on the rural-county margins.

The "positive coverage depresses Republicans" part is not supported by anything I found. He uses "depress the vote" only about a Marist poll (a War Room clip, Oct 21). He also posted on Oct 19 that psyops almost never work.

Expect pushback from his own posts. He says repeatedly that the early vote confirms the polls' likely-voter models (Oct 15, 16 and 22). He warns against reading the early vote as a polling miss (Oct 15). He says the missing MAGA voter is not coming (Oct 15). He also says that outside Texas, Republicans who do not show up in the early vote do not surge on Election Day (Ep. 120, Oct 12). Section 3 has all of these.
verdict.note: All in-window posts read (Oct 8 to 24); paraphrased.
